result.summary:
Independently re-derived from docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md itself (not CODE-DESIGNER's step-01-code-designer.json result.summary).

1. ZERO IMPLEMENTATION CODE. `grep -n '```' docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md` finds exactly two fenced blocks: lines 114-120 (the `getWaitlistPosition(db, eventId, registrationId): Promise<number | null>` export signature, a bare `;`-terminated declaration, no body) and lines 231-238 (the `registration: { ... }` interface addition, two `string;` field declarations, no assigned values). Both are structure/types only. The position rule itself (§2.2, §2.3) and the reply-composition change (§3.2) are stated entirely in prose/ordered lists, explicitly declining to write the comparison/count logic as executable code even in one-line form -- exactly the discipline `.claude/agents/code-designer.md` calls out (REQ-016/REQ-017's prior FAILs). No stray hex color, no CSS, no handler/route implementation code anywhere in the document.

2. TOKEN REFERENCES. This is a bot/backend design with no rendered UI surface -- `grep -n 'var(--\|--color\|--space\|--font'` over the file returns zero matches. No color/spacing/typography token is referenced, invented, or needed; nothing to check against docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/tokens.css, consistent with REQ-020's precedent for the same surface.

3. AC2/REQ-022 SCOPING JUDGMENT. Read §0 and §6 open question 1 in full. Weighed against REQ-018's 'target list doesn't exist yet' and REQ-019 §8 open question 3's 'interim substitute verification' precedents: this is the same shape of problem (an AC's own stated verification method names a feature -- withdraw -- that depends_on this very requirement and therefore cannot exist yet) and the same class of resolution (name a precise, runnable substitute rather than build a stand-in feature). I judge option (b) correct, not merely acceptable, for a reason stronger than 'it matches precedent': the property AC2 actually asserts is a property of getWaitlistPosition alone -- 'recomputed fresh from live `admission` state on every call, with no cache and no write to the other row' -- and by the function's own signature (`getWaitlistPosition(db, eventId, registrationId)`) it receives no argument describing *why* a row is no longer `'waitlisted'`. A direct SQL `UPDATE registrations SET admission = ...` and a real REQ-022 withdraw call are therefore indistinguishable to this function -- both change the same column read by the same `WHERE admission = 'waitlisted'` filter. Building an internal-only withdraw primitive (option a) would not exercise any code path this design doesn't already cover; it would only add product-shaped surface (confirm-first gate, seat-freeing, audit action) that isn't this requirement's to invent, exactly as §0 reasons. Verified this reasoning against the actual code, not just the design's prose: `apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts` lines 173-214 (`registerForEvent`'s write path) confirm `admission` is set once at INSERT time from `outcome.kind` and is never referenced again by any other function in that file -- there is no other mechanism in the current codebase that would make 'how admission changed' observable to `getWaitlistPosition`. I therefore do not find a gap here: the AC's literal 'withdrawing' language names an eventual UI trigger, not an additional code path this design would need to build to make the property true. Residual note (non-blocking, for the record): when REQ-022 ships, its own TEST-DESIGNER should re-run this same AC2 property once through the real withdraw handler as an integration check, since REQ-021's substitute only proves the query side, not the full user-facing flow -- worth a line in REQ-022's test spec, not a defect in this design.

4. POSITION QUERY CORRECTNESS -- traced against the actual schema (apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts). Confirmed lines 242-299: `registrations.id` is `uuid(...).primaryKey().defaultRandom()` (line 245), `createdAt` is `timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow()` (lines 275-277, i.e. Postgres `timestamptz`, microsecond precision), `admission` is a `notNull` enum column (line 252), and `registrations_waitlist_order_idx` (lines 290-292) is exactly as claimed: `index(...).on(table.eventId, table.createdAt).where(sql`${table.admission} = 'waitlisted'`)` -- a partial index on `(event_id, created_at) WHERE admission = 'waitlisted'`, with its own comment (line 288) stating it was built 'for the waitlist-ranking query.' The design's §2.2/§2.3 'ahead' definition (`created_at` strictly earlier, OR equal `created_at` with lower `id`) is a total order over the filtered row set: `created_at` is a real (if theoretically collidable at microsecond granularity) total preorder, and `id` -- a uuid with no semantic ordering, correctly flagged as such in §2.3 -- breaks every tie because two distinct rows cannot share both `created_at` and `id`. A total order over a fixed, well-defined set (rows with `event_id = X AND admission = 'waitlisted'` at the moment of the read) yields exactly one rank per row with no possibility of two rows computing the same position or two callers disagreeing about the ranking of the same snapshot -- the count-ahead formulation (count of strictly-ahead rows, plus one) is algebraically identical to a `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY event_id ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC)` window restricted to one row, as the design itself notes. Concurrent reads: since the function performs one read of the target row (id/admission/created_at) and one count query with no intervening write of its own, two concurrent calls each see some consistent snapshot of `registrations` (ordinary MVCC read semantics, no new consistency requirement introduced) -- a possible skew between two concurrent callers' answers if a write lands between their two reads is inherent to 'recomputed live, never cached' (the explicit design goal, PRD 5/PRD 13 criterion 8) and is not a bug the design needs to prevent. The `id` tie-break is necessary in principle (timestamptz can theoretically collide at the microsecond boundary under concurrent inserts) even though not expected in practice -- the design states this correctly (§2.3) rather than assuming collisions can't happen.

5. PURE-READ / NEVER-CACHED CHECK. §2.2 describes exactly one `SELECT ... LIMIT 1` (step 1) and one `SELECT count(*)`-shaped query (step 3) -- no `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`.set(`/`.values(` construct anywhere in §2. §2.4 explicitly enumerates every existing interface in this codebase that could have carried a stored position (`RegistrationOutcome`, `RegisterForEventResult`, `EventRecord`) and states none gains a position/rank field; confirmed against the actual `RegistrationOutcome`/`RegisterForEventResult` types in `apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts` (lines 34-43, 104-106) -- neither has nor gains such a field in this design. No new table/column/index is proposed (§7); this matches `apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` having no `position`/`rank` column anywhere in `registrations`.

6. AC-TO-DESIGN-ELEMENT MAP (§8), re-derived independently rather than trusted: AC1 (position shown on waitlisted confirmation) maps to §3's handler wiring, verified against the actual `handlers/registration.ts` (lines 60-116) -- `outcome.registrationId` is populated unconditionally by `registerForEvent`'s write path (domain/registration.ts lines 210-213) for the waitlisted branch, so §3.1's `getWaitlistPosition(db, eventId, outcome.registrationId)` call has a real value to consume; concrete, not TBD. AC2 -- addressed above (item 3), concrete substitute test named. AC3 (no stored position, `git grep`-checkable) -- addressed above (item 5), concrete and checkable today. AC4 (unbounded waitlist) -- verified against `decideRegistrationOutcome` (domain/registration.ts lines 48-74): row 8 (`return { kind: "waitlisted" }`) is the unconditional fallback with no preceding count-based rejection anywhere in the function, confirming §5's 'proof of absence' claim is actually true of the current code, not just asserted.

No open question in §6 is a silently-resolved ambiguity -- all four are named as open, with the design's own chosen answer stated and reasoned, per the role's 'flag, don't silently resolve' rule. No TBD/deferral language found anywhere in the document.

Verdict: PASS. No check failed.

issues.description: Non-blocking, for the record per WF-02's rework/issue framing: when REQ-022 (withdraw) ships, its own TEST-DESIGNER should add one end-to-end verification of AC2's property (second person's position 2→1 after a real withdraw call, no write to their row) exercised through the actual withdraw handler rather than only the direct-SQL substitute this design names -- REQ-021's substitute proves the query side of the property correctly, but not the full user-facing flow. This is a note for REQ-022's test design, not a defect in docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md.
